subject.title: Session context bloat: bootstrap files re-injected every turn, wasting 20-30% tokens

question: Should OpenClaw change the global bootstrap-injection default, or keep continuation skipping as an explicit performance mode while separately fixing any restart or transcript defects?
rationale: The merged behavior deliberately preserved the existing default, while current evidence shows runtime-dependent semantics and incomplete proof that one global default is safe for changed workspace instructions, recovery, compaction, and non-Codex runtimes.

options.title: Keep opt-in pending cross-runtime proof
options.body: Retain the present default, document the performance mode, and require focused evidence for restart, compaction, changed-file, and non-Codex behavior before changing compatibility semantics.

options.title: Adopt continuation skip as default
options.body: Change the default only with an explicit migration and regression matrix proving that required instructions are reintroduced after compaction, restart, and relevant workspace changes.

options.title: Split correctness from optimization
options.body: Track restart or duplicate-transcript defects under the umbrella investigation while treating global token-policy changes as a separate product proposal.

recommendation.title: Keep opt-in pending cross-runtime proof
recommendation.body: Retain the present default, document the performance mode, and require focused evidence for restart, compaction, changed-file, and non-Codex behavior before changing compatibility semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current continuation-skip safety contract and are the strongest history-based routing candidate for its default and lifecycle invariants.
